title: One sale is luck. Ten sales are a business.

beats.say: Your first sale feels like success. But it’s just luck.
beats.visual: extreme close of a single $20 bill under a dim desk lamp, shallow depth of field

beats.say: One customer paying you $100 proves nothing.
beats.visual: silhouette of a hand exchanging a crisp bill against a rain-slick street at night

beats.say: How do you know it wasn’t a fluke?
beats.visual: empty neon-lit underpass, fog rolling in, low angle looking up at abandoned carts

beats.say: Most think: if it works once, it’ll work again. But markets don’t care about your hope.
beats.visual: towering office buildings at twilight, a lone figure walking away, extreme wide shot

beats.say: Here’s the test: sell to 10 strangers, not your friends.
beats.visual: crowded city plaza, slow pan over faceless crowd, sodium streetlights blur

beats.say: At a 1% yes-rate, 100 reach-outs a day for 100 days nets 100 customers.
beats.visual: desk with a laptop, hands typing, extreme close on keyboard, cold fluorescent light

beats.say: One sale is luck. Ten is a pattern. A pattern is a business.
beats.visual: high angle shot of a rolling suitcase on wet asphalt, tracks leading into distance

beats.say: But most quit after the first yes. Or the first no.
beats.visual: abandoned storefront, broken neon sign, blue hour lighting

beats.say: What’s your next move: more of what works, or pivot to fantasy?
beats.visual: ridge line at dusk, a tiny hiker against the vast horizon

beats.say: Do more of what already works, then make it better, then try something new.
beats.visual: extreme close of a hand tightening a bolt on a machine, industrial setting

beats.say: The catch: active income first. Passive comes later, if ever.
beats.visual: empty highway at night, tail lights fading into distance, low angle

beats.say: Ten sales to strangers prove you’re in business. Then the real work starts.
beats.visual: sunrise over a city skyline, silhouettes of cranes, high angle

beats.say: Follow for the money rules nobody taught you.
beats.visual: tall glass skyscraper at golden hour, reflected in a puddle, extreme low angle

caption: One sale proves luck. Ten sales to strangers prove a business. The test you’re not taking.
description: The graduation test for your first stage of income: consistent first sales to strangers, not friends. Here’s the rule to prove it’s a business, not luck.
first_comment: What’s one thing you’ve sold that wasn’t a fluke?
